scope: Distinct queue-role consent retirement and duplicate-verification monotonicity; no native room-making execution
findings: Server registry previously pruned on authenticated BEGIN/ACK/RELEASE only. A disconnected owner and no further requests could leave expired records until another admission sweep.
Accepted owners retained private PENDING/AGREED metadata without independent timeout.
An identical VERIFY arriving after AGREED could rewrite the receipt to PENDING; future queue phases must not inherit that downgrade.
Adding one-shot expiry creates timer churn unless server admission also limits fresh serial/immediate release cycles. Caller-side request deduplication alone is insufficient server authority.
implementation: Server schedules one bounded original-phase/deadline retirement callback for PENDING and one on first AGREED transition. Exact token/current phase/deadline checks and atomic registry retirement preserve successor state; RELEASED is delivered to original owners without world queries.

Owners schedule matching canonical token/serial/roster/roles/dependencies/context/deadline/expiry/phase retirement. Matching old-machine private metadata may be removed after locality changes; this publishes no movement state. Pending timeout cannot clear AGREED, and old token cannot clear a successor.
Duplicate accepted PENDING verification adds no timer. Duplicate VERIFY of an exact live AGREED receipt only repeats ACK; it never downgrades phase. Duplicate AGREED results return before scheduling.

Private server64-entry initiating-vehicle admission journal permits one accepted BEGIN per30seconds, independent of serial/owner changes. Expired admission entries are pruned during authenticated admission; overflow refuses. Existing32live-episode bound remains.
limits: CBA scheduling latency, clock changes, network delivery, ownership changes and actual disconnect cleanup remain unrun. Timer delay is not a physical deadline guarantee; cancellation can conservatively revoke an unchanged receipt early after clock changes.
Admission bounds new timers; queued callbacks under scheduler starvation and aggregate frame-time cost require measurement. No recurring query or new permanent controller is introduced.
These functions issue no hold, movement, reverse, path or speed commands. Consent is not HOLD/READY or queue success; native executor/dependency/handback and verified reverse remain incomplete.
